column12: Judgement on the comparator, under the house convention. Ibrance with letrozole is the first-line regimen in FourLight-3's control arm, Pfizer's own oral CDK inhibitor, and the drug atirmociclib is built to replace. The case against: the other two comparators in the same arm run lower per beneficiary in 2024: Verzenio $94,026 and Kisqali $88,305. Ibrance's figure is highest partly because its patients are longer on therapy. Ibrance was also selected for Medicare price negotiation (maximum fair price from 2027), so its gross figure will overstate what the class nets in Medicare by the time atirmociclib launches. Taking Kisqali instead would cut the price by 31%. No published annual list price for atirmociclib exists

column12: Judgement on the filter. The label will reach first-line endocrine-based candidates. The case for a lower figure: the 0.843 includes endocrine monotherapy for frail patients and patients relapsing within a year of adjuvant aromatase inhibitor, who would take fulvestrant rather than letrozole. I found no US source for either share. The window also ends in 2019, when chemotherapy use was falling. Applied to incidence this is about 54,800 first-line starts a year. Applied to the book's 160,000 prevalence it gives an opening stock of 134,900, most of whom are already on a CDK4/6 inhibitor or past first line. See untreated_carryover_pct. Second reader: the Goyal cohort is women aged 65 and over (median 74) selected on initiating systemic therapy, so 0.843 is a share of treated older patients, not of every incident case; younger patients are likelier to get a CDK4/6 inhibitor and less likely to be untreated, which cut in opposite directions

column12: Judgement: atirmociclib is assumed to reach the share the third CDK4/6 entrant measurably holds, nine years after its approval and with an overall-survival label. Two assumptions sit under it. First, that the CDK4/6 class covers the whole eligible first-line pool. That overstates it, since some endocrine first-line patients take monotherapy. Second, that the beneficiary share is a first-line share. Part D beneficiaries also include second-line and, from September 2024, some adjuvant Kisqali. The case for higher: FourLight-3 is head to head against a CDK4/6 inhibitor, and Pfizer has reason to move Ibrance's 44.3% class share to a patented successor as Ibrance's negotiated Medicare price and generic entry arrive. A win would make a share well above Kisqali's plausible. The case for lower: a fourth entrant faces generic palbociclib and ribociclib by the mid-2030s
